title: Inside visualize-architecture-flow
summary: Start with the authoring contract, follow the executable validator, then inspect its data structures and failure boundaries. This atlas explains the pinned reference skill; it does not claim to visualise your application yet.

source.scope: The visualization reference, wrappers, dedicated Python validator and global installation/hygiene context.
source.excluded: Other skills, private user repositories, target applications and production runtime behaviour.

evidence.label: Skill entrypoint and global reference dependency
Documented evidence-first, state-first workflow and manual browser checks
Global installer supplies the shared reference and Codex script

entities.label: Feature explanation request
entities.summary: The developer selects a feature, use case or issue and a source branch. The default audience is a developer new to that feature.

entities.label: SKILL.md entrypoint
entities.summary: A small routing instruction directs the assistant to read a shared reference before building HTML. It is not an extraction or rendering program.
facts: The repository-wide installer supplies that location. Copying only this wrapper does not create a portable standalone skill.

entities.label: Authoring workflow
entities.summary: A prescribed process for an assistant to investigate one feature and create a state-driven HTML explanation. The procedure is documentation, not an implemented generation pipeline.
facts: Evidence → domain state → scenarios → visual encoding → HTML.
Normal and evidence-backed failure/recovery paths are expected.
invariants: An implementation claim needs evidence. Planned paths remain separate from current behavior.

entities.label: Authoring assistant
entities.summary: The agent performs the investigation, interpretation and HTML authoring described by the reference. No reusable diagram renderer or model extractor is supplied in this skill folder.
facts: The instructions describe how to work, not a deterministic pipeline implementation.
The supplied code only lints the generated HTML.

entities.label: Standalone HTML output
entities.summary: The intended output embeds CSS, JavaScript and SVG. State, steps, controls and source references are authored for the selected feature.

fields.name: baseState
fields.meaning: Produces the initial domain state for replay.

fields.name: scenarios
fields.meaning: Each step has explanation, evidence, animation metadata and a patch function.

invariants: External resources are disallowed by the output contract, except ordinary evidence hyperlinks.
That contract is stronger than the supplied regex validator can enforce.

entities.label: HTML validator CLI
entities.summary: A Python text-pattern linter checks required, forbidden and recommended strings, then reports errors and warnings. It does not parse a DOM or execute the HTML.
invariants: A PASS means no configured error pattern failed. It does not establish architectural truth or offline behavior.

entities.label: Manual browser review
entities.summary: The reference separately requires real browser checks: viewport layouts, scenarios, seeking, cancellation, reduced motion and console errors. This is prescribed manual/agent work, not implemented by the Python validator.

entities.label: Collect feature evidence
entities.summary: Trace entrypoints, use cases, domain logic, adapters, infrastructure, tests, configuration and documented implementation status.

entities.label: Define domain state
entities.summary: Identify authoritative state, messages, artifacts, leases, invariants and recovery. This is intentionally done before HTML.

entities.label: Describe state transitions
entities.summary: Build ordered normal and failure/recovery scenarios. Recompute a selected step by replaying patches from a fresh initial state.
invariants: Replay is deterministic only if the authored baseState and patch functions are themselves deterministic.
A linear example is not a concurrency proof.

entities.label: Choose visual semantics
entities.summary: Use roles, boundaries, meaningful geometry, labelled operations and selective edges. Keep live state consistent with causal order.

entities.label: html argument
entities.summary: argparse converts the argument to pathlib.Path. main expands ~ and resolves it before calling validate.

fields.name: html
fields.meaning: Input file location; not HTML content. No schema is attached to this value.

entities.label: validate(path)
entities.summary: Initialises two diagnostic lists; checks the file and extension; reads UTF-8; runs three collections of regex checks; returns the lists.
invariants: A missing file returns immediately with an error.
A wrong extension records an error but does not stop later checks.
Read and decode errors are not caught here.

entities.label: Decoded HTML text
entities.summary: The complete UTF-8 file is searched as one string, including comments, script source and prose. There is no distinction between live markup and quoted or commented markup.

fields.name: text
fields.meaning: Whole decoded file; no DOM/token tree or resource inventory is constructed.

invariants: A pattern hit in a comment is still a hit.

entities.label: required patterns
entities.summary: Six regexes search for a doctype, language, charset, viewport, inline CSS and a script tag. Absence adds an error.
facts: The code tests raw textual presence, not live DOM presence.

entities.label: forbidden patterns
entities.summary: Eight regexes search for selected dependencies, iframe, TODO literals and full-width parentheses. Presence adds an error.
facts: Patterns differ in coverage: scripts are caught only when src= has no whitespace around =.
Relative image/CSS URLs, protocol-relative images, SVG images and JavaScript networking are outside these patterns.
TODO and full-width parentheses are style rules, not self-containment properties.

entities.label: recommended patterns
entities.summary: Four patterns look for reduced motion, an ARIA live region, SVG and playback-labelled buttons. Their absence adds warnings only.

fields.name: recommended
fields.meaning: Recommendation label → regex whose absence produces a warning.

invariants: Finding these strings does not establish that the controls work.

entities.label: matches(pattern, text)
entities.summary: Calls re.search with IGNORECASE and DOTALL, then returns whether a match exists. Context is irrelevant to this function.

fields.name: text
fields.meaning: Whole source text of the HTML document.

fields.name: return
fields.meaning: True when any substring matches, including text in comments.

entities.label: Diagnostic result
entities.summary: The output is a tuple of error and warning lists, rather than a parsed document, resource graph or architecture model.

fields.name: errors
fields.meaning: Missing required pattern, matching forbidden pattern, or file/extension error.

invariants: Warnings alone never produce the explicit failure return code.

entities.label: CLI report and exit
entities.summary: Prints diagnostics. Returns 1 when errors is non-empty and 0 otherwise. A decoding exception bypasses this explicit report policy.

fields.name: warnings
fields.meaning: Printed and counted but not part of the fail condition.

fields.name: return
fields.meaning: 1 for reported validation errors; 0 for no reported errors.

entities.label: All markup inside a comment
entities.summary: A controlled test wraps an otherwise passing scaffold in an HTML comment. Every configured required/recommended string is present in the source, but not as live document content.
facts: This fixture was accepted with zero errors and zero warnings in the local probe run.
The probe results are included in reports/upstream-results.json.
invariants: Fixture observations are not measurements of real application behavior.

entities.label: No live scaffold content
entities.summary: The browser treats the outer comment as a comment. The scaffold inside it does not create live SVG, script, style or playback controls. The browser still supplies its normal implicit document structure.
facts: This is the explanatory contrast in the fixture, not a general statement about every passing document.

entities.label: UTF-8 decoding exception
entities.summary: Invalid UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError at read_text. The validator does not return diagnostics and main does not catch the exception.

relations.label: Caller interprets bool
relations.summary: The helper returns a bool; each caller decides whether true or false adds an error or warning. The helper itself does not modify the diagnostic lists.

relations.label: Interpret as HTML comment
relations.summary: Explanatory contrast: browser parsing does not instantiate the elements enclosed in the comment; the regex helper still sees their text.

views.title: Overview: instructions, artifact and checks
views.question: What does the existing skill actually provide?
views.summary: The architecture is a documented authoring procedure plus a small executable linter. The assistant supplies the interpretation and bespoke HTML. The browser checks are a separate required activity.
takeaways: The strongest idea is state-before-animation, not animation itself.
This package is a feature explainer, not an implemented multi-level architecture explorer.
Drill into the authoring workflow or the executable validator; both retain links to the pinned source.

views.title: Documented authoring workflow
views.question: How should an assistant build the explanation?
views.summary: These nodes are prescribed activities, not callable functions. The reference deliberately puts domain state and scenarios before visual design and HTML.
takeaways: Collect operational evidence, including failure and recovery.
Use a fresh initial state when seeking through a scenario.
Do not confuse a requirement in a document with an implemented automation.

views.title: Executable validator: control and data flow
views.question: What happens to the HTML file when the script runs?
views.summary: Three dictionaries are checked sequentially in the code. Their parallel placement here exposes their different effects, not concurrent execution. Select a scenario to inspect those checks in order.
takeaways: Whole-file text is the input, not an HTML syntax tree.
Required/forbidden checks add errors; recommended checks add warnings.
Only a non-empty errors list controls the explicit failure code.

views.title: Validator data structures and ownership
views.question: Which values are produced, consumed and mutated?
views.summary: The matcher is a pure bool-returning helper. validate owns and mutates the diagnostic lists. main consumes the returned tuple. Select any type for its fields and meaning.
takeaways: The boolean alone has no failure meaning; its caller decides the policy.
errors and warnings have the same representation but different operational consequences.
A regex dictionary is not a resource-dependency inventory.

views.title: A passing lint result can describe an empty page
views.question: How can the linter accept a document with no live controls?
views.summary: A controlled fixture places all required and recommended strings inside one comment. The unchanged script accepts it with zero diagnostics. The browser/regex contrast is deliberately marked illustrative.
takeaways: A text hit does not establish a live element.
The original reference still requires browser validation; its Python helper is not a replacement.
The defect belongs to the validator, not to regex matching itself: it applies the wrong representation to the claim.

views.title: Failure before diagnostic checks
views.question: What survives an input decoding failure?
views.summary: There is no error-to-diagnostic conversion around read_text. Invalid UTF-8 raises before the regex dictionaries are evaluated. The local probe confirmed UnicodeDecodeError.
takeaways: A function that usually returns diagnostics can still raise.
Draw this as an exception path, not a normal validation error.
Source links show both the unguarded read and the absence of a catch in main.
